name: Remove Noise from Microscopy Image using FFT Bandpass Filter
description:
A microscopy image has been corrupted by both high-frequency noise (from the camera) and low-frequency uneven illumination (background gradient). Your goal is to clean this image using Fiji's FFT Bandpass Filter.

1. Open the noisy image located at `~/ImageJ_Data/raw/noisy_blobs.tif`.
2. Measure the image statistics (Analyze > Measure) to establish a baseline (note the Standard Deviation).
3. Apply the 'Bandpass Filter' (Process > FFT > Bandpass Filter...).
   - You need to filter out large structures (low frequency) to fix the uneven background (try approx 40 pixels).
   - You need to filter out small structures (high frequency) to remove the pixel noise (try approx 3-5 pixels).
   - Ensure you do NOT suppress stripes (set to None).
4. Save the resulting filtered image to `~/ImageJ_Data/results/filtered_image.tif`.
5. Create a simple CSV report at `~/ImageJ_Data/results/bandpass_filter_results.csv` comparing the 'Before' and 'After' statistics. It must include columns for 'Condition' (Before/After), 'Mean', and 'StdDev'.

Success is determined by a significant reduction in the Standard Deviation (noise) while preserving the mean intensity of the objects.
